newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, brisk spec selling.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, brisk spec selling.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled weaker after a breach of support triggered sell stops and pressured the benchmark December contract to four-week lows.
Technically-driven speculative selling pressured the most-active month below key 74.00 cents to a low of 73.60 cents, where trade buying stymied further losses.
The contract fell to 73.25 cents on July 15.
December closed down 0.80 cent on the day at 73.78 cents, having ranged from 74.50 to 73.50 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.18 to 0.86 cent lower.
Market sources expect December to fall to its next downside target seen at the contract low of 73.20 cents.
"I think we will see it over the next week because the market can't seem to stay up," a trader said.

Today's losses were blamed on weak technicals and expectations for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's crop progress report to reveal an improved crop. The USDA will issue its weekly report at 1600 EDT.

Beneficial weather across the cotton belt was also keeping the market under pressure, industry sources said. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's weekly crop progress report is expected to show the the crop has improved.
Lower CBOT soybean prices also contributed to weakness in NYCE cotton futures, traders said.
An estimated 12,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Friday's official 3,652 lots.
